issues.failure_explanation: The paper repeatedly claims that the ranks obtained from Tucker-ALS on the small Chebyshev coefficient tensor C are nearly optimal and essentially equal to those of grid-based Tucker-ALS. No theorem relates the ranks of C to the ranks of the discretized function, and no grid-based Tucker-ALS computation is shown for comparison. The only rigorous result (Prop. on f-hat versus f-tilde) controls the Frobenius error of C, with a sqrt(m1 m2 m3) loss. That is a different norm from the grid or sup-norm accuracy that defines the grid-based optimal rank. The 'strong theoretical guarantees ... almost optimal rank' attributed to Tucker-ALS are not true of ALS, which is a local iteration, and are not proved here. The reported rank tables are never compared with grid-based ranks.

failure_location.quote: This leads to nearly optimal Tucker rank parameters which are close to the results for well established Tucker-ALS algorithm

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to what is shown (ranks of the coefficient tensor at tolerance epsilon). Alternatively, add a rank-comparison argument or numerical grid-based Tucker-ALS ranks for the same examples, and correct the Tucker-ALS 'guarantee' remark.
issues.overall_effect: The central selling point (near-optimal ranks without grid-based Tucker decomposition) is supported only by heuristic statements, so the rank-optimality claims in the abstract, introduction, and conclusions are unreliable.
issues.title: Claim of nearly optimal ranks, comparable to grid-based Tucker-ALS, is not established
issues.why_classification: A contained rewording and added comparison data or argument suffice, and the construction and its error bounds are untouched. The headline claim must nevertheless be weakened or newly supported.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with the core tensor $\boldsymbol{\beta}^0$ and  the orthogonal Tucker factor matrices $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} \in \R^{n_\ell \times r_\ell^0}$

issues.failure_explanation: The matrix V G G^T V^T is n_l x n_l of rank at most r_l^0 < n_l, so it cannot equal the identity I_{n_l}. Orthonormality of the factor V G requires (VG)^T(VG) = G^T V^T V G = G^T G = I_{r^0}. That holds only if G has orthonormal columns, a hypothesis the proof never invokes ('substituting ... proves the orthogonality'). The only content actually proved is the associativity V = beta0 x (VG).... The statement that the resulting Tucker ranks are 'reduced (quasi-optimal)' is also not derived.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that G^(l) has orthonormal columns and replace the displayed identity with G^T V^T V G = G^T G = I_{r^0}.
issues.overall_effect: The orthogonality part of the proposition is justified by a false identity. The factorization itself is trivially correct.
issues.title: Proof of hybrid-to-Tucker proposition asserts a false orthogonality identity
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction using the existing orthogonality hypothesis repairs the proof, and all claims survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: note that the inner product should be properly weighted
which forms a sequence of orthogonal polynomials on $[-1,1]$ with respect to the weight $w(x) = 1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$

issues.failure_explanation: The polynomials v_j = sum_i V_{ij} T_{i-1} satisfy <v_i,v_j>_w = (pi/2)(delta_ij + V_{0i} V_{0j}) when the columns of V are Euclidean-orthonormal, because ||T_0||_w^2 = pi while ||T_k||_w^2 = pi/2 for k >= 1. Euclidean orthonormality of V therefore does not give weighted orthogonality. Example: columns (1,1,0,...)/sqrt2 and (1,-1,0,...)/sqrt2 give <v_1,v_2>_w = pi/4 != 0. The count is also wrong: v^(l) has r_l entries, not r_l^0, and G does not enter this proposition.

failure_location.quote: appear to be the set of $r_\ell^0$ orthogonal polynomials

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the orthogonality claim, or require V^T D V = I with D = diag(2,1,...,1) (up to the pi/2 normalization) and correct the count to r_l.
issues.overall_effect: The orthogonality assertion for the functional factors, and the abstract's 'orthogonal' two-level algebraic Tucker tensor obtained by discretizing the Chebyshev polynomials on a grid, are not justified.
issues.title: Claimed orthogonality of the Chebyshev Tucker factor polynomials is false (weighted norms, wrong count)
issues.why_classification: The orthogonality statement is auxiliary, nothing later depends on it, and the fix is a local rescaling or removal.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark states that the computational cost of the RHOSVD-based algorithm is O(mR) and concludes it is 'always preferred'. The paper's own complexity estimate, and its proof (truncated SVDs of the side matrices cost O(mR min{m,R}), core reconstruction costs O(R r^3)), shows the cost is larger than O(mR). Only the memory is O(mR). The universal preference is also not supported.

failure_location.quote: the memory and computational cost are both $\mathcal{O}(mR)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State memory O(mR) and computational cost O(mR min{m,R} + mR log m + R r^3), and replace 'always preferred' by 'preferred in the regime where ...'.
issues.overall_effect: The stated cost advantage of the RHOSVD algorithm is misstated and inconsistent with the proved estimate. The qualitative comparison is not materially affected.
issues.title: Remark claims O(mR) computational cost for the RHOSVD route, contradicting the complexity proposition
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one sentence, consistent with the existing proposition, restores the claim.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited RHOSVD bound (error <= ||xi|| times a sum of tail singular values of the side matrices) holds for canonical tensors with normalized canonical vectors, as in the paper's own CP definition. The canonical vectors of C, c_k = W q_k, are Chebyshev coefficients of spline values on the Chebyshev grid and are not normalized. The scaling by 2/(m-1) and the weights in W, and the change of sampling points, alter their norms. The weights xi_k therefore do not match the unnormalized c_k, and the bound with ||xi|| is not implied. The sigma_k^(l) are also never defined in the lemma statement.

failure_location.quote: The desired result then follows from the standard error analysis of the RHOSVD truncation \cite[Theorem 2.5]{khoromskij2009multigrid}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize the vectors c_k^(l), absorb the norms into xi~_k = xi_k prod_l ||c_k^(l)||, define sigma_k^(l) as the singular values of the normalized side matrices, and restate the lemma and theorem with ||xi~||.
issues.overall_effect: The RHOSVD truncation term in the lemma and in the final error theorem (and the adaptive-rank remark based on it) is unproven as stated. The correct weights could differ substantially from ||xi||.
issues.title: RHOSVD error bound applied to unnormalized canonical vectors of the coefficient tensor
issues.why_classification: The fix is a standard renormalization, but it changes the quantities in the lemma and theorem and requires re-deriving the bound with the correct weights.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $C_4 m^3(m+n) + C_5 m^3 + C_1 m^3 \log m + C_2 m^4 + C_3 m^4 |\log \varepsilon|$
does not require storage of the discretized function on the fine 3D-grid

issues.failure_explanation: The univariate estimate O(m+n) does not extend 'similarly' to the trivariate case. A tensor-product cubic spline of the n x n x n array F requires solving tridiagonal systems along n^2 lines in each of 3 directions, plus reading all n^3 entries, so setup costs at least Omega(n^3). Evaluation at m^3 Chebyshev nodes adds O(m^3). The true cost is O(n^3 + m^3), which is not bounded by C_4 m^3(m+n) when n is large relative to m (for example n=4096, m=129). The input F of this algorithm is the full fine-grid tensor, so the remark that the algorithms in both cases need no fine-grid storage is also false for it.

failure_location.quote: Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the spline cost by O(n^3 + m^3) in the complexity statement and its proof, and restrict the mesh-free and no-fine-grid-storage claims to the functional and CP-input algorithms.
issues.overall_effect: The complexity bound for the grid-input algorithm is understated. The mesh-free and 'avoid the n^3 grid' claims do not hold for it, and the comparison with the CP-input algorithms is affected.
issues.title: Cost estimate for the full-tensor algorithm ignores the n^3 data and mesh-free claim fails for it
issues.why_classification: The correction is local, but the stated complexity changes and an advertised property (mesh-free) is lost for one of the four algorithms.
